To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the isogeometric approach is able to solve plane stress/strain boundary element problems with inclusions that exhibit elastic and plastic behavior.

1) the use of lower order singular kernels for the volume integrals allows the use of a single set of NURBS basis function for the geometry and the field variables; 2) the use of NURBS for the geometry of the inclusions and the field variables allows the use of the same basis functions for all variables; 3) the use of the NURBS basis for all variables is advantageous because the geometry of the domain is exactly described by these basis functions; and

(1) the isogeometric approach for boundary element analysis of inclusions is very promising, (2) the use of lower order singular kernels in the domain term is essential for the success of this method, (3) the use of NURBS basis for the geometry of the inclusions is essential for the accuracy and robustness of the method, (4) the use of higher order singular kernels in domain term leads to inaccurate results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical solution of the boundary value problem of the elasto-plastic inclusion problem.
the development and implementation of an isogeometric Boundary element method for the simulation of elasto-plastic domains with inclusions.

the development of a novel Boundary Element method, that can be applied to domains with inclusions with arbitrary geometry, and inelastic material behavior, and that can be used for the solution of practical engineering problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method works very well and that the results are in good agreement with analytical solutions and finite element solutions.
the proposed method is a very promising approach to the isogeometric analysis of inclusions with elasto-plastictic material properties.
the presented approach is a very promising alternative to existing methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
isogeometric Boundary element analysis is possible for domains with inclusions with inelastic material properties.
the isogeometric BEM is a very promising method to solve boundary value problems with inclusions.
we have presented a method that can be used for modeling inhomogeneous materials with different elastic properties and material non-linearity using the same basis functions for geometry and analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Kernels with lower singularity allows to reduce the number of unknowns in the system of equations.
the use of Kernels of lower order in the domain term is a viable alternative to the use of Kriging methods.
isogeometric Boundary element analysis is a viable method for the solution of problems with inelastic inclusions.
